strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#43178 via pandas DataFrame.sum overflow/skipna=False all-NaT paths that exercise the ndarray branch of nanops._wrap_results. The provided tests should fail on the buggy revision 6850d49c8de2 (silent saturation / incorrect raise) and pass on the fix PR 66227.

tzdata (optional; README says only required on Windows/Emscripten)

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 6850d49c8de2, the test_sum_timedelta64_overflow_raises assertion (expecting OutOfBoundsTimedelta for df.sum over overflowing timedelta64) fails because df.sum returns a saturated int64-max-like result with only a RuntimeWarning instead of raising the pandas OutOfBoundsTimedelta. Also, on the buggy revision, test_sum_timedelta64_all_nat_skipna_false (all-NaT, skipna=False) fails because the overflow guard is not mask-aware and/or can falsely trigger, causing an incorrect raise or incorrect non-NaT result; on the fixed revision (PR 66227 applied), both tests pass: overflow genuinely raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta, and all-NaT with skipna=False returns NaT (dtype m8[ns]) for both axis=0 and axis=1.
strategy.numerical_probe: The test probes timedelta64 reduction overflow and mask-aware overflow handling by using an int64 half-max construction in nanoseconds, ensuring the sum over three values overflows int64 bounds after internal conversion; and separately summing an all-NaT m8[ns] frame with skipna=False to ensure NaT positions are exempt from overflow checking.

input_output_examples.input: half = np.iinfo(np.int64).max // 2; arr = np.array([half, half, half], dtype="m8[ns]"); df = DataFrame({"a": arr, "b": arr, "c": arr}); df.sum(axis=0, skipna=True/False)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Raises no OutOfBoundsTimedelta; may instead produce a saturated (i8max-derived) timedelta64 result and/or only a RuntimeWarning (exact value not required by the test).
input_output_examples.expected_output: Raise pd.errors.OutOfBoundsTimedelta with message matching "overflow in timedelta operation".

input_output_examples.input: nat = np.array(["NaT","NaT","NaT"], dtype="m8[ns]"); df = DataFrame({"a": nat, "b": nat, "c": nat}); result = df.sum(axis=axis, skipna=False)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Test fails because either an incorrect overflow is raised or result is not entirely NaT (the test asserts result.isna().all()).
input_output_examples.expected_output: result.dtype == "m8[ns]" and result.isna().all() for axis=0 and axis=1.

oracle.why: The tests use exception type/message and boolean NaT checks (dtype and result.isna().all()), so no numeric tolerance comparison is required.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: test_sum_timedelta64_overflow_raises fails: df.sum(axis=axis, skipna=skipna) does not raise pd.errors.OutOfBoundsTimedelta on the overflowing timedelta64 frame because the overflow guard is missing/insufficient in the ndarray branch, leading to silent saturation (with only a RuntimeWarning). Additionally, test_sum_timedelta64_all_nat_skipna_false fails on the buggy revision because skipna=False all-NaT reductions can falsely trip overflow logic due to mask-unawareness, yielding either an incorrect exception or a non-NaT result; the test’s dtype and result.isna().all() assertions would fail.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After applying PR 66227’s fix, both tests pass: genuine overflow raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta for both axes and both skipna values, and all-NaT with skipna=False returns NaT for both axes.
